title: Boundary-unit factorization in a regular local ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], hence Noetherian, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ be members at distinct positions of a regular system of parameters of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], with $r\ge0$. Then $A$ is an integral domain with unique factorization: every nonzero element is a unit times a finite product of prime elements, uniquely up to order and association. Each $t_i$ is prime. Put $T=t_1\cdots t_r$, with empty product $1$, and write $A[1/T]$ for localization at the powers of $T$. An element $f\in A$ becomes a unit in $A[1/T]$ if and only if $f=u\prod_{i=1}^r t_i^{a_i}$ for a unit $u\in A^\times$ and integers $a_i\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 0AG0, lemma-regular-local-UFD (lines 36800–36858): a regular local ring is a UFD; its proof first explains that a member of a regular parameter system is prime. The localization-unit clause is the elementary consequence of unique factorization detailed in report.md, rather than an assertion of the normal-crossings equivalence lemma.

proof.text: The regular-local domain instance [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] gives IsDomain A. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] at the maximal ideal to obtain IsRegularRing A, then the already proved source-library theorem [lem-trf-regular-local-regular-ring-ufd] gives UniqueFactorizationMonoid A. This discharges the UFD induction by reuse, without restating it.

For a position i of t, permute that parameter to the head using t.get i :: t.eraseIdx i. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], the permuted list is a regular system of parameters and a regular sequence. Its head is a nonzerodivisor, hence nonzero since A is nontrivial. The same theorem with c=1 makes the quotient by its singleton ideal regular local. By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] the quotient is a domain, so the nonzero head is prime. Apply this to each selected position.

Put T=prod_i t_i. All factors are prime, hence nonzero, so T is nonzero (also when r=0). Mathlib IsLocalization.Away.algebraMap_isUnit_iff says f becomes a unit exactly when f divides T^n for some n. Prove the forward monomial assertion by UniqueFactorizationMonoid.induction_on_prime. Zero cannot divide a nonzero power of T. A unit has all exponents zero. For p*f, both images are units; induction factors f. The prime p divides T^n, hence T and hence some t_i. As t_i is prime, p is associated to t_i. Absorb the association unit into the induction unit and increase exponent i by one. The finite-product identities give the required equality.

Conversely, the image of the unit u is a unit. Each selected t_i divides T, so IsLocalization.Away.isUnit_of_dvd makes its image a unit. Products of their natural powers are units, giving the reverse implication. For r=0 the product is 1, the prime step has no possible index, and the assertion is precisely that f is a unit.

lean.statement: theorem regularLocalUFDBoundaryFactorization (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A] (t : List A) (ht : IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters t) (r : ℕ) (ι : Fin r → Fin t.length) (hι : Function.Injective ι) : IsDomain A ∧ UniqueFactorizationMonoid A ∧ (∀ i : Fin r, Prime (t.get (ι i))) ∧ (∀ f : A, IsUnit (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (∏ i : Fin r, t.get (ι i))) f) ↔ ∃ u : A, IsUnit u ∧ ∃ a : Fin r → ℕ, f = u * ∏ i : Fin r, (t.get (ι i)) ^ (a i))
